# dsh-panel-fold
**Fold the DSH sidebar's global panel icons into the More menu — give your workspace and session lis
t its vertical space back.**
中文说明 · MIT · a DeepSeek Harness web client plugin
DSH's left sidebar devotes a fixed block near the top to the *global panel* launchers — Plugins, Aut
omated tasks, XD Pool, Context insights, MCP connectors, WSL, Library, and so on. Every plugin that
registers a panel adds one more 36px row there. With a handful of plugins installed, that block alon
e eats seven or eight rows, and the workspace / session list underneath gets squeezed into a narrow
seven or eight rows, and the workspace / session list underneath gets squeezed into a narrow strip.
This plugin folds those rows into the single **More** button that already sits at the bottom of that
block. Panels stay one click away; the list above your sessions does not.
| Before | After |
Both screenshots are of the same window with the same plugins enabled — the only difference is the f
screenshots are of the same window with the same plugins enabled — the only difference is the fold.
> Verified on DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop profile, Windows). The fold survives `Ctrl+R`, and folded-vs
-expanded round-trips in place without a reload.
## What you get
- **One row instead of eight.** The panel block collapses to `⋯ More`. The workspace list directly b

elow gains roughly `7 × 36px` of height.
- **Nothing becomes unreachable.** Every panel is still in
the More menu, and opening one behaves exactly as before (`selectPanel`, current selection preserved

). `plugins` is untouched by design — it is the row ui-sidebar itself refuses to unpin.
- **A one-li
ne toggle.** The last row of the More menu is `Show global panel icons` / `Fold global panel icons i

nto More`. Click it and the rows come straight back, no reload, no restart.
- **The choice sticks.**
Stored in `localStorage` under `dsh-panel-fold:mode` (`collapsed` | `expanded`), so it survives ref

resh, restart, and plugin reload.
- **Folded by default.** Installing the plugin is the opt-in.

## How it works
No patching of ui-sidebar, and no dependency on its hashed CSS class names (those change between rel
hing of ui-sidebar, and no dependency on its hashed CSS class names (those change between releases):
1. The web client half watches the DOM with a `MutationObserver` and marks the panel-list `<nav>` —
matched first by its `aria-label` (`全局面板` / `Global panels`, i.e. ui-sidebar's `t("panels.label")`),
falling back to the structural signal *"a `<nav>` that contains a `button[aria-haspopup="menu"]` an

d at least two direct child buttons"*.
2. One CSS rule hangs off a class on `<html>`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The last child of that `<nav>` is the More button, so only it remains.
3. The toggle row registers i
nto the `sidebar.panellist.actions` slot, which ui-sidebar renders inside the More menu.
### Why not the built-in unpin mechanism?
ui-sidebar does have a "pin / unpin panel" mechanism (`setPinned`), and unpinning a panel removes it
s row while keeping it in the More menu. But `setPinned` is only reachable through the `sidebar.pane
llist.actions` owner props, and that slot only mounts *while the More menu is open* — there is no wa
y to apply a pin state at startup. The CSS route needs no such hook, and it is what lets the plugin
honour a persisted preference on first paint.
## Reversibility

- **Temporary:** sidebar `More` → `Show global panel icons`. Instant.
- **Permanent:** disable or un
install `dsh-panel-fold`. The `<style>` tag and the `<html>` class go with it, leaving the sidebar e

xactly as shipped.
- **Disable without uninstalling:** append to your user patch layer:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

## Related work
Two other plugins touch the same block. Both are stable, MIT, and worth a look if you want more than
r plugins touch the same block. Both are stable, MIT, and worth a look if you want more than a fold:
- `ACGsu/dsh-sidebar-panel-fold` — **the closest neighbour.** It adds its own "collapse panels" row
above the list; collapsing turns the whole block into a single summary row (active panel icon + name
) that opens a popover listing every panel, and the state persists through DSH's host settings chann
el rather than `localStorage`. If you would rather have a dedicated summary row with the active pane

l's name on it, use that one.
- `LoktLin/dsh-sidebar-tidy` — a much broader take: it hides the brand
row, the new-session button, the panel block *and* the footer settings behind one "exit minimal mod
e" button, and adds workspace colour blocks. If you want the whole sidebar stripped down, use that.
`dsh-panel-fold` deliberately takes the smallest possible slice: it adds **no new row** — it reuses
the More button ui-sidebar already renders at the bottom of the block — it changes nothing else in t
he sidebar, and it keeps the client half under 7 KB with no host-side code at all.
